parts.label: (a)(i)(ii)
parts.technique: Binomial distribution probability calculations
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly covers calculating probabilities using the binomial distribution; these sub-parts are direct binomial probability calculations at the expected depth.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Independent events / binomial probability product
parts.reason: Combines binomial probability from (a) with independence of events (S3.1) to find probability all 5 packets satisfy condition; standard technique, no exclusion applies.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for binomial proportion - stating hypotheses
parts.reason: S5.2 explicitly covers stating hypotheses in terms of population proportion p for a binomial proportion test.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Hypothesis test using an approximation (Poisson main method, Normal approximation as full-mark alternative)
parts.reason: The main mark scheme method uses a Poisson approximation, which is not mentioned anywhere in the specification statements and so is out of spec. However, the mark scheme's SC1 special case explicitly allows a Normal approximation to the binomial (N(5,4.75^2) with continuity correction) to earn the same full 6 marks (M1A1;M1A1;dM1A1). Normal approximation to a binomial with continuity correction is explicitly in S4.2, so a fully in-spec method can earn full marks.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculation
parts.reason: Uses the Poisson distribution, which is not named or covered anywhere in the specification statements; no in-spec alternative method exists for this calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculation
parts.reason: Same as (a): requires Poisson distribution, not covered by any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Poisson property / memorylessness reasoning
parts.reason: Requires knowledge that Poisson events occur independently/randomly and reasoning based on Poisson probability from (a); Poisson not in spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Poisson modelling for expected profit calculation
parts.reason: Requires setting up Po(0.9) and solving for n; entirely dependent on Poisson distribution which is not in spec.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Hypothesis test for a Poisson rate
parts.reason: This is a hypothesis test for a Poisson parameter lambda; S5 only covers tests for binomial proportion and Normal mean, not Poisson rate, so this is out of spec.

parts.label: b

parts.reason: Requires working with a probability density function, explicitly excluded by S4.2 ('Knowledge of the probability density function is not required').

parts.label: c

parts.reason: Depends on pdf knowledge and calculating E(Y^2) for a continuous random variable, not covered/excluded by S4.2.

parts.label: d

parts.reason: Uses out-of-spec E(Y^2) from part (c) and pdf-based variance; not covered by any statement.

parts.label: e

parts.reason: Requires integrating the pdf to get cdf and solving for a percentile; pdf knowledge explicitly excluded (S4.2).

parts.label: i(ii)
parts.technique: Sampling distribution of the range of a discrete random sample
parts.reason: The question explicitly requires finding the 'sampling distribution' of B, a named concept the specification statements do not mention; this makes it out of spec per the explicit rule that unmentioned named concepts like 'sampling distribution' are out.

parts.technique: Properties of a cumulative distribution function for a continuous random variable
parts.reason: Requires understanding of cdf/pdf for a general continuous random variable; S4.2 excludes knowledge of the pdf and its derivation, and no statement covers general continuous distributions' cdf.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Deriving a pdf from a cdf by differentiation
parts.reason: Directly requires pdf knowledge, excluded by S4.2.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: Continuous uniform distribution is not mentioned anywhere in the specification statements (only binomial and Normal distributions are covered in S4), so this is out of spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Binomial-type probability calculation using probabilities derived from out-of-spec continuous distributions
parts.reason: Although the final combinatorial calculation resembles a binomial-style calculation, it relies entirely on probabilities (121/625 etc.) derived from the out-of-spec pdf/cdf and uniform distribution in earlier parts, so it only makes sense after out-of-spec work.

parts.label: i(ii)
parts.technique: Normal approximation to binomial with continuity correction; solving resulting quadratic for p
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers approximating B(n,p) by N(np, np(1-p)) with continuity correction, and standardising to find probabilities/parameters. The algebraic manipulation to derive and solve the quadratic uses standard quadratic-solving skills (P2.3). All required techniques (normal approximation to binomial, continuity correction, standardising, solving quadratics) are covered by statements, though the overall multi-step depth is unusually high for this topic.
